subject: Observability license transition sprint and renewal sequencing
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Observability license transition sprint and renewal sequencing

Team —

We have a tight window coming up on multiple observability contracts (Datadog, Grafana Cloud, Sentry retention add-on). Rather than treat each renewal independently, I propose a short "transition sprint" to:
- lock down contract milestones and responsibilities
- sequence vendor outreach to minimize overlap and egress costs
- identify quick-win reductions (retention tiers, indexed log reduction) before renewal cutovers

I've attached an initial workbook (redwood_datadog_RFP-responses.xlsx) that compiles current end dates, committed spend, and preliminary vendor quotes. Key constraints: Datadog term ends 2026-11-15 (auto-renew if no action), Grafana quote expires 2026-09-20, Sentry retention add-on quote needs legal review.

Ask: Can we run a 5-business-day coordination sprint starting 2026-09-07? Proposed outputs: vendor negotiation plan, revised cost model, and a lightweight risk register for data egress and compliance.

If you agree, I will: coordinate calendar slots, consolidate vendor asks, and originate outreach to the three vendors in parallel with staged sequencing.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Procurement & Vendor Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_datadog_RFP-responses.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 sheets)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability license transition sprint and renewal sequencing

+1 on the sprint. A couple of tactical thoughts:
- Sequence Datadog first (auto-renew risk + largest line item). Try to push to a 60-day notice if possible.
- Grafana Cloud can be negotiated for a pilot re-tier (move hot logs to Loki indexed tier). Quote expiry is tight — we should lock terms or request extension right away.
- Sentry: retention add-on is the lowest $$ but highest product impact (alerts/ingest). We should ask Sentry for a usage-based cap rather than fixed retention to avoid billing surprises.

I'll take the Datadog negotiation play. Can we add a quick cost sensitivity table to the workbook with tokenized scenarios?

Ben
Sr. Finance Manager, Observability Costing

Subject: Re: Observability license transition sprint and renewal sequencing

Thanks — I pulled vendor quotes and attached the Grafana PDF (grafana-cloud-pricing-quote.pdf). High-level notes:
- Grafana: they offered a 10% onboarding credit but the retention tiers are rigid in the quote. We can ask for a 30-day quote hold while we finalize scopes.
- Datadog: RFP responses (spreadsheet) include a suggested discount band if we move to a 12-month committed pool. However, transition to an alternate pipeline (Loki/Grafana) has one-time migration costs estimated in the workbook.
- Sentry: their retention addendum draft (sentry-retention-addendum-draft.docx) flags an ingest-rate clause that would retroactively reprice if we exceed retention thresholds — legal should review.

I'll flag the migration costs in the cost sheet and add a small section for risk (egress, timeline slippage). Happy to own Grafana extension asks.

—Marissa
Vendor Strategy Lead

Attachments: grafana-cloud-pricing-quote.pdf
